notes:
Batch AF (colecalciferol, calcium carbonate/colecalciferol, ferrous sulfate/folic acid, folic acid, ascorbic acid, vitamin B complex, iron polymaltose/vitamin B complex, calcium glubionate). BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). Every quote checked FOUND against the cached page text.
SOURCES / SUBSTITUTIONS: (1) colecalciferol: no UK 2000 IU/ml drop; used Fultium-D3 Drops 2740 IU/ml (emc-6861, text last revised 2015), THORENS 10 000 IU/ml drops (emc-7044) and Colecalciferol 3000IU/ml oral solution (emc-8091). Exact 50,000 IU soft capsule found only on MHRA Products (PL 20416/0805, blob PDF). (2) calcium carbonate/colecalciferol: no UK 600 mg Ca + 200 IU tablet; used Accrete D3 (600 mg Ca + 400 IU, emc-2766) and Adcal-D3 Caplets (300 mg Ca + 200 IU, emc-4723). AUDIT 2026-10-17: the calcium-only formulation (ccd-calcium-only-600, emc-1295) that had been added for the clinic row "caltrate / calcium carbonate 600mg" was REMOVED; that clinic row must be remapped to medicine calcium-carbonate (batch G) in clinic-map.json. (3) ferrous sulfate/folic acid: exact UK product (Fefol Spansule, MHRA PL 48669/0001, 47 mg elemental iron + 500 micrograms folic acid). (4) folic acid 5 mg: exact (emc-14604). (5) ascorbic acid: no UK 1000 mg tablet; UK 500 mg tablet SmPC used (emc-101277); its stated adult max is 1000 mg/day. (6) vitamin B complex: clinic composition is thiamine 2 mg + riboflavin 2 mg + pyridoxine 2 mg + calcium pantothenate 3 mg + niacinamide 20 mg (clinic-map.json). Nearest UK product Vitamin B Compound Strong (MHRA PL 20416/0410: thiamine 5 mg, riboflavin 2 mg, nicotinamide 20 mg, pyridoxine 2 mg) has NO calcium pantothenate. AUDIT: kept as a partial match; formulation note says so, dosing/paediatric scoped to the UK tablet, lactose excipient rules removed. (7) iron polymaltose/vitamin B complex: NO UK iron polymaltose oral product (emc search 'polymaltose' re-run 2026-10-17: no results; MHRA index searched earlier). AUDIT 2026-10-17: converted to availability no-uk-product (the earlier fill from a ferrous fumarate syrup used a different iron form); rules [], removed from iron-preparation and polyvalent-cation groups, emc-2822 source removed. (8) calcium glubionate/lactobionate syrup: no UK product or UK calcium syrup; used Calvive 1000 effervescent tablets (calcium lactate gluconate + carbonate, 1000 mg Ca, emc-1191) for calcium-class content only. AUDIT: dosing/paediatric scoped to the UK tablet ('use the clinic label for the syrup dose'); administration not-stated; excipient/citrate-driven rules (PKU, glucose, severe renal impairment citrate caution, aluminium interaction) removed.
CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES (kept as separate items/rules): separation intervals - Accrete D3: levothyroxine/thyroid hormones and iron 2 h; quinolones 2 h before or 6 h after; tetracyclines 2 h before or 4-6 h after. Adcal-D3 caplets and Adcal: minimum 4 h before taking calcium. Calvive: tetracyclines 2 h before or 4-6 h after. Levothyroxine SmPC (emc-435): 4-5 h. Ciprofloxacin SmPC (emc-7257): cipro 1-2 h before or at least 4 h after. Fefol: iron not within 1 h before or 2 h after antacids/calcium; levothyroxine 2 h. Renal stones and hypercalciuria: absolute CI in Accrete D3 4.3 vs relative CI in Adcal-D3/Adcal. Kidney stones in colecalciferol: absolute in Fultium/3000IU/50k capsule, but THORENS limits it to patients with current chronic hypercalcaemia. Severe renal impairment threshold eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73m2 is stated only in the 3000IU/ml solution SmPC; others give no number. Vitamin D 50,000 IU capsule SmPC: high strength not recommended in pregnancy/lactation; SPS: loading doses up to 300,000 units over 6-10 weeks can be used in breastfeeding with infant monitoring; SPS pregnancy: 1000-2000 units daily for deficiency.
NOT MAPPED TO RULES (no master-list member or membership not sourced): cardiac glycosides/digitalis, phenytoin, barbiturates, rifampicin, colestyramine, orlistat, paraffin oil, bisphosphonates, levodopa, penicillamine, dimercaprol, desferrioxamine, chloramphenicol, lithium, concomitant parenteral iron (Fefol 4.3 CI). Imidazole antifungals (vitamin D activation) not mapped: batch AG now has group imidazole-antifungal, but every member in the master list is a skin/mouth/vaginal product, so the engine would never apply a systemic rule to them (AUDIT 2026-10-17). Folic acid and methotrexate: SmPC says folic acid may interfere with methotrexate; SPS (sps-folic-mtx, also used by batch F) says folic acid is routinely co-prescribed in RA (usually not on methotrexate day) - kept as info.
NEW: group vitamin-d (colecalciferol, calcium-carbonate-colecalciferol). Conditions added: sarcoidosis, pseudohypoparathyroidism, haemoglobinopathy, cobalamin-deficiency, malignant-disease, hyperoxaluria. Reused conditions from other batches: hypercalciuria, vitamin-d-overdose, primary-hyperparathyroidism, severe-renal-failure-no-dialysis, immobilisation-osteoporosis, hereditary-sugar-intolerance, haemolytic-anaemia, repeated-blood-transfusions, paroxysmal-nocturnal-haemoglobinuria, swallowing-difficulty, phenylketonuria (G); nephrocalcinosis, severe-renal-impairment (A/Z); renal-impairment; peanut-soya-allergy (D); galactose-intolerance-lactase-deficiency (B); megaloblastic-anaemia (F). The fultium 2740 IU/ml drop table uses a U+0096 dash character; two dosing quotes contain it verbatim.
